extract_bench_v12.py run on the full 12Mb region (chunked 500kb at a time, single-threaded): loads reads, computes per-locus counts, Binomial LLR, and Poisson-Binomial (PB) LLR for all 10,975,654 scored loci. This is NOT a fair like-for-like against the external callers' calling-only runtimes above, because it performs full read-level PB scoring for every locus rather than only the ~0.15% the frozen router actually sends to PB in production use -- it exists to build the evaluation cache, not to represent cascade production latency.

Once binomial_llr/pb_llr are cached, applying the frozen router+thresholds (arms_on_mask) and computing accuracy metrics over 10.9M loci took well under 1 second in-process (pure numpy). This IS representative of the router's actual marginal cost.
